name: The 1975
label: Dirty Hit
lede: Four kids from Wilmslow who spent a decade under five other names, then got a record deal for £20 and kept making the records they wanted: long ones, strange ones, and in 2022 a short, plain one that Pitchfork ranked No. 33 of the year.

eras.title: Five names before the right one
eras.text: Four school friends in Wilmslow, Cheshire, played under a run of names nobody remembers fondly while Matty Healy figured out he was the singer. The 1975 is the name that finally stuck.

years.h: Wilmslow High School: a band with no singer
years.p: Guitarist Adam Hann recruited Matty Healy to drum in a band with bassist Ross MacDonald. When the singer they tried out, Elliott Williams, left after one rehearsal, Healy took over the vocals.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, [[George Daniel|22bb3c13-87b5-46ac-8dc9-553b6579c2e6]] later took over the drum stool, which is how the four-piece that still exists today took shape. The group played under a stack of names before settling: Me and You Versus Them, Those 1975s, Forever Drawing Six, Talkhouse, the Slowdown, Bigsleep and Drive Like I Do.

Healy has kept the last one alive: during the 2020 shutdown he teased new music under the name Drive Like I Do.

eras.title: £20, a Kerouac scribble and four EPs
eras.text: A manager starts a label and signs the band for pocket change, then a run of EPs, a Zane Lowe co-sign and support slots with Muse and the Rolling Stones make a debut album feel inevitable.

years.h: Manager Jamie Oborne starts Dirty Hit and signs them for £20
years.p: The band settled on The 1975 after scribbles in Healy's copy of Jack Kerouac's On the Road, dated 1 June.
years.xp:
Per Wikipedia, Jamie Oborne founded Dirty Hit as an independent label to release the band, and the £20 figure is the price the label paid to sign them. The name comes from handwriting in Healy's paperback of Jack Kerouac's On the Road.

Dirty Hit went on to release the band's whole catalogue, often alongside Polydor.

years.h: Facedown EP: "The City" gets BBC Introducing airplay
years.p: The first EP put the band on Radio 1's new-music radar before they had a manager's office to speak of.

years.h: Sex EP, and Zane Lowe starts playing it
years.p: The Sex EP gave the band its first champion on national radio in DJ Zane Lowe.

years.h: Music for Cars EP: "Chocolate" reaches No. 19 in the UK
years.p: The third EP's lead single was their first UK chart single, at No. 19, and a video went up for it.

years.h: Opening for Muse at Emirates Stadium
years.p: On 26 May they played a London football stadium as the support act, months before their first album.

years.h: Hyde Park, supporting the Rolling Stones
years.p: On 13 July 2013 a band with EPs and no album played in front of the Rolling Stones' crowd.
years.cap: The 1975 performing at the Glastonbury Festival in 2025 · Wikimedia

years.h: The 1975: a sixteen-track debut that goes to No. 1
years.p: Recorded with producer Mike Crossey at Motor Museum in Liverpool, it topped the UK Albums Chart on 8 September 2013.
years.xp:
Wikipedia reports it was made between June and September 2012 and in March 2013, and that it spawned seven singles including "Sex", "Robbers" and "Chocolate". Metacritic gives it 67/100 from 17 reviews. Wikipedia also says it reached platinum status in the US, with 1 million copies sold by June 2018.

Gigwise's Ashley Clements called it possibly the best indie LP of the year; Clash gave it 8/10.

years.big: Glitchy R&B to big 80s powerpop to mid 90s soul
q: Glitchy R&B to big 80s powerpop to mid 90s soul
years.h: A record that won't sit in one genre
years.p: That is how Healy described the debut's palette, and critics kept filing it under electropop, indie pop, pop rock and emo.
years.xp:
Wikipedia notes that NME dubbed the band's influence on indie pop "Healywave", naming Pale Waves, Fickle Friends and The Aces among the acts influenced.

The band's own list of influences includes Talking Heads, My Bloody Valentine, Ride and Michael Jackson, and Healy names film-maker John Hughes as his biggest influence.

eras.title: Bigger than the bedroom
eras.text: Coachella, the Royal Albert Hall, a social-media blackout and then a second album with a title that takes a breath to say. The band becomes a two-continent No. 1 act.

years.h: Coachella, then the Royal Albert Hall
years.p: Their first big US festival slot came in April 2014, the same month they played London's Royal Albert Hall.
years.cap: Ross MacDonald of The 1975, October 2014 · Wikimedia

years.h: Every social account wiped, then back the next day in pink
years.p: Posts vanished on 1 June 2015 and returned the next day with a new look for the second album.
years.xp: Wikipedia describes the deletion as a publicity stunt. The accounts came back with an altered look, and the second album was announced that October.

years.h: I Like It When You Sleep: No. 1 in the UK and the US
years.p: The second album topped the charts in both countries and brought "Love Me", "UGH!", "The Sound" and "Somebody Else".
years.xp: Per Wikipedia it also reached No. 1 in Canada, Australia and New Zealand, earned a Grammy nomination for its box-set packaging at the 59th Grammys, a Mercury Prize nomination, and was named NME's Album of the Year for 2016.
play: I Like It When You Sleep, for You Are So Beautiful yet So Unaware of It

eras.title: Sincerity is scary
eras.text: Healy went to rehab in the middle of the third album, and the record that came out of it traded irony for plain talk about screens, love and recovery. It won the Brit.

years.src: Wikipedia: A Brief Inquiry into Online Relationships
years.h: A Brief Inquiry into Online Relationships: the first without Crossey
years.p: Healy and George Daniel produced it themselves across eight studios in London and Los Angeles, and it entered at No. 1 in the UK.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says sessions ran from June 2017 to September 2018 and were interrupted when Healy went to a rehabilitation clinic in Barbados for heroin addiction. The record deals with digital communication, recovery and mental health, and critics often compared it to Radiohead's OK Computer. Metacritic scores it 83/100 from 29 reviews.

Singles included "Give Yourself a Try", "Love It If We Made It", "TooTimeTooTimeTooTime" and "Sincerity Is Scary".
play: A Brief Inquiry into Online Relationships
Love It If We Made It

years.src: Wikipedia: A Brief Inquiry into Online Relationships · Wikipedia: The 1975 (band)
years.h: British Album of the Year at the Brit Awards
years.p: A Brief Inquiry into Online Relationships won the top album prize at the 2019 Brits.
years.xp: The record also earned a Mercury Prize nomination, and "Give Yourself a Try" was nominated for Best Rock Song at the 62nd Grammys.

years.h: Greta Thunberg opens the next album, proceeds to Extinction Rebellion
years.p: The track "The 1975" is a speech by the climate activist over ambient music, and its proceeds went to Extinction Rebellion.

years.h: Headlining Reading and Leeds
years.p: The band topped the bill at the festival, a long way from the Shepherd's Bush Empire shows of 2013.

eras.title: A long record into a locked-down world
eras.text: The fourth album is sprawling and lands in the first months of a pandemic that cancelled the tour behind it. Healy and Daniel spend the quiet producing other people.

years.h: Notes on a Conditional Form: a fourth No. 1 with guests
years.p: It was their fourth straight UK No. 1 and featured Phoebe Bridgers on "Jesus Christ 2005 God Bless America" and FKA twigs on "If You're Too Shy (Let Me Know)".
years.xp: Wikipedia reports it was also No. 1 in Australia and No. 4 in the US, and was certified silver in the UK in December 2020. The 2020 tour was postponed and then cancelled during COVID-19. NME named the band its Band of the Decade at the 2020 NME Awards.
play: If You're Too Shy (Let Me Know)

years.h: Healy and Daniel produce beabadoobee's Our Extended Play
years.p: During the pause the pair produced and co-wrote the EP, and appeared on the No Rome and Charli XCX track "Spinning".

eras.title: Shorter, plainer, funnier
eras.text: A fresh start with Jack Antonoff in the room, a short album about love, and then a controversy that ends a tour. The band heads to a hiatus and a Glastonbury headline.

years.h: Every account goes dark again
years.p: The band deactivated its social media on 14 February 2022 and came back on 1 June with a new era.

years.h: "Part of the Band" arrives as the first single
years.p: The song was followed by postcards mailed to fans with the tracklist.

years.src: Wikipedia: Being Funny in a Foreign Language · Album of the Year: Being Funny in a Foreign Language · Metacritic: Being Funny in a Foreign Language · Pitchfork: The 50 Best Albums of 2022
yt: Part of the Band (Official Live Performance)
years.h: Being Funny in a Foreign Language: Pitchfork gives it 8.0 and ranks it No. 33 of 2022
years.p: Recorded from January to May 2022 at Electric Lady in New York and Real World in Wiltshire, with Jack Antonoff producing alongside Healy and George Daniel. It runs 43 minutes.
years.xp:
Pitchfork scored the album 8.0 (Wikipedia and Album of the Year list it as 80/100), and later put it at No. 33 on its 50 best albums of 2022. Metacritic gives it 82/100 from 16 critics, and Album of the Year lists the Guardian and Rolling Stone at 80.

It went to No. 1 in the UK, Australia and Ireland and No. 7 on the US Billboard 200. Singles were "Part of the Band", "Happiness", "I'm in Love with You", "All I Need to Hear", "About You" and "Oh Caroline". It was nominated for British Album of the Year at the 2023 Brits.

years.h: Madison Square Garden, live-streamed on Twitch
years.p: The sold-out show got five-star reviews from Rolling Stone, NME, the Observer, the Telegraph, the Evening Standard and Metro.

years.h: "About You" goes to radio
years.p: The album track was serviced to radio on 23 December 2022 and became a live high point, performed again at Glastonbury.

q: We can't let the kids down because they're not the problem.
years.src: Wikipedia: Good Vibes Festival · Wikipedia: The 1975 (band)
years.h: Healy kisses Ross MacDonald in Malaysia and the festival is shut down
years.p: After Healy criticised Malaysia's anti-LGBT laws from the Good Vibes Festival stage, authorities ordered the rest of the three-day event cancelled.
years.xp:
Wikipedia reports that Healy and MacDonald kissed onstage and that Malaysian authorities cited remarks against local culture. The band was banned from Malaysia and later cancelled dates in Taiwan and Indonesia; the festival organisers later sued for £1.9 million, according to Wikipedia. Healy said the band's decision to play was a mistake.

Activist Peter Tatchell argued the focus should be on Malaysia's anti-gay laws. Some Malaysian LGBTQ+ people said they feared reprisals, per the Good Vibes Festival page.

years.h: Third Reading and Leeds headline: the debut turns ten
years.p: The band played a 10th anniversary set of The 1975 to mark a decade since the self-titled album.

years.h: The Still... At Their Very Best tour: Healy announces a touring hiatus
years.p: At the opening show in Sacramento, Healy said the band would take a break from touring afterwards.

years.h: Live recording at Manchester's AO Arena
years.p: A show recorded on 17 February 2024 was later released as Still... At Their Very Best (Live From The AO Arena, Manchester, 17.02.24).

years.h: Healy and George Daniel on Charli XCX's Brat remix record
years.p: Manchester billboards advertised the band's collaboration with Charli XCX and Jon Hopkins on "I might say something stupid".

eras.title: One show, a pyramid, and a sixth record
eras.text: After a year off the road, the band takes the Glastonbury headline slot and confirms a sixth album is nearly done.

years.h: Glastonbury Pyramid Stage headline, their only show of 2025
years.p: Manager Jamie Oborne said in May that Glastonbury would be the band's only concert of the year, and that a sixth album was being made.
years.xp:
The Guardian's Alexis Petridis called the band "world-class" and the set "hugely impressive", per Wikipedia. NME published the full setlist and set highlights.

In December 2025, Healy said at an event in Gateshead that the album would be called DOGS and that they had made two albums, one of which might come out separately.
years.cap: The 1975 performing at the Glastonbury Festival in 2025 · Wikimedia

years.h: Healy names the sixth album: DOGS
years.p: He confirmed the title at Gateshead College and said the band had made two albums.
